title: Customers From The US
description:
Report the `name` of every customer whose country is `US`.

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT name FROM customers WHERE country = 'US';
hint: A customer with a NULL country is not equal to 'US' — NULL comparisons are never true.
outputExplanation: Ada and Cy are from the US. Bo is from the UK and Di is from India.

title: Products Over 50
description:
Report the `name` and `price` of every product priced above 50.

Name the columns `name` and `price`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT name, price FROM products WHERE price > 50;
hint: Straight WHERE filter; products with a NULL price drop out on their own.
outputExplanation: Keyboard ($80) and Desk ($300) are priced above $50. Mouse ($25) and Lamp ($45) are not.

title: Orders By Status
description:
Report how many orders exist for each status.

Name the columns `status` and `orders`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS orders FROM orders GROUP BY status;
hint: GROUP BY puts all NULL statuses into a single group of their own.
outputExplanation: There are 4 completed orders, 1 cancelled order and 1 pending order.

title: Customers Per Country
description:
Report how many customers signed up from each country.

Name the columns `country` and `customers`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM customers GROUP BY country;
hint: One row per distinct country, including the NULL group.
outputExplanation: Two customers are from the US, one from the UK and one from India.

title: Product Categories
description:
Report each distinct product category, excluding NULL.

Name the column `category`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT DISTINCT category FROM products WHERE category IS NOT NULL;
hint: DISTINCT keeps NULL as a value, so filter it out explicitly.
outputExplanation: The products fall into two categories: Tech and Furniture.

title: The Priciest Product
description:
Report the highest product price in the catalogue.

Name the column `max_price`. The result is exactly one row.
solutionSql: SELECT MAX(price) AS max_price FROM products;
hint: MAX ignores NULLs and still returns one row when the table is empty.
outputExplanation: The most expensive product is Desk at $300.

title: Orders Placed In 2022
description:
Report the `id` and `order_date` of every order placed during 2022.

Name the columns `id` and `order_date`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql: SELECT id, order_date FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2022-01-01' AND order_date < '2023-01-01';
hint: A half-open range on ISO date strings is both correct and index-friendly.
outputExplanation: Orders 1 through 5 were placed in 2022. Order 6 was placed in 2023.

title: Units Sold Per Product
description:
Report each product's name and the total number of units of it that appear in order items. Products that were never sold must appear with `0`.

Name the columns `product` and `units`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT p.name AS product, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity), 0) AS units
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.id
GROUP BY p.id, p.name;
hint: LEFT JOIN keeps unsold products; COALESCE turns the resulting NULL sum into 0.
outputExplanation: Mouse and Lamp each sold 6 units, Keyboard sold 3 units, and Desk sold 1 unit.

title: Products Never Sold
description:
Report the `name` of every product that has never appeared in any order item.

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT p.name
FROM products p
LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON oi.product_id = p.id
WHERE oi.id IS NULL;
hint: Anti-join: LEFT JOIN then keep the rows where the right-hand side stayed NULL.
outputExplanation: All four products have been sold at least once, so no products are reported. A hidden test adds a product that was never sold.

title: Value Of Each Order
description:
For every order that has at least one item, report the order id and its total value — the sum of `quantity * unit_price` across its items, rounded to 2 decimals.

Name the columns `order_id` and `total`. Return the result in any order.
hint: You never need the orders table here — order_items already carries the order id.
outputExplanation: Order 1 is worth $185, order 2 is $300, order 3 is $180, order 4 is $75, order 5 is $80, and order 6 is $140.

title: Completed Orders Per Customer
description:
Report every customer's name and how many **completed** orders they have. Customers with none must still appear, showing 0.

Name the columns `customer` and `completed_orders`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT c.name AS customer,
       COUNT(CASE WHEN o.status = 'completed' THEN 1 END) AS completed_orders
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
GROUP BY c.id, c.name;
hint: Putting the status test in the WHERE clause would delete the zero-order customers. Move the condition inside the COUNT instead.
outputExplanation: Ada has 3 completed orders and Cy has 1. Bo and Di have none.

title: Average Price Per Category
description:
Report each product category and its average price, rounded to 2 decimals. Ignore products with no category.

Name the columns `category` and `avg_price`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT category, ROUND(AVG(price), 2) AS avg_price
FROM products
WHERE category IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY category;
hint: AVG skips NULL prices, so a category with only NULL prices averages to NULL.
outputExplanation: Furniture products average $172.50 each, while Tech products average $52.50.
